claims.explanation: Tyrphostin-AG-99 is an EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor, and its selective killing pattern is best explained by dependence on EGFR signaling. Sensitive lines are enriched for EGFR mutations (HCC4006, NCIH1650, KYSE270) and for lineages where EGFR is a known driver (lung, esophageal, thyroid). Conversely, resistant lines often lack EGFR alterations and instead harbor mutations in downstream effectors such as KRAS, BRAF, NRAS, or MET, which can bypass EGFR inhibition.

features.basis: Activating EGFR mutations predict response to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors; observed in multiple sensitive lines.
High EGFR expression increases dependence on EGFR signaling and sensitivity to EGFR inhibitors.
KRAS mutations activate downstream MAPK signaling and confer resistance to EGFR inhibitors; enriched in resistant lines.
BRAF mutations bypass EGFR dependence and are common in resistant melanoma and colorectal lines.
NRAS mutations activate MAPK pathway independently of EGFR; seen in resistant lines.
MET alterations can provide alternative RTK signaling and resistance to EGFR inhibition; observed in resistant HGC27.
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT signaling downstream of EGFR, reducing dependence on EGFR; common in resistant lines.
PIK3CA mutations activate PI3K pathway and may bypass EGFR blockade; present in several resistant lines.
ERBB3 mutations can sensitize to EGFR inhibitors by altering heterodimerization; observed in sensitive SNUC5.
TP53 mutations are common in both groups but may contribute to resistance; not specific.
